pages.title: Definition and scope of pharmacology

concepts.label: Scope of pharmacology
concepts.detail: Study of substances interacting with living systems through chemical processes; includes sources, properties, dosage forms, administration, ADME, actions, uses and adverse effects.

pages.title: Pharmacology, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics

concepts.label: PK versus PD
concepts.detail: PD concerns what a drug does to the body; PK concerns what the body does to a drug.
concepts.rationale: Explicit general definition, mechanism, route distinction or functional relationship.

pages.visualNotes: Image-only chart: drug = exogenous chemical molecule producing biological response/effect. Pharmacology = science of drugs (Pharmacon drug; logos discourse in). PD (dynamis power) = what drug does to body. PK (kinesis movement) = what body does to drug.

pages.title: Enteral routes

concepts.detail: Swallowed oral drug enters GI tract; sublingual under tongue and buccal between gums/cheek enter bloodstream directly; rectal absorption through rectum.

pages.title: Oral route advantages

concepts.label: Oral advantages
concepts.detail: Convenient, self-administered, pain free, absorption along GI tract, cheap, low infection risk. Source also mentions charcoal for overdose; do not generalize to all poisons.
concepts.rationale: Explicit general definition, mechanism, route distinction or functional relationship.

pages.title: Oral route disadvantages

concepts.label: Oral limitations
concepts.detail: Incomplete absorption, pH effects, first pass via portal vein/liver, acid/digestive destruction, mucosal irritation, slow emergency onset, taste and inability to use in unconscious patients.
concepts.rationale: Explicit general definition, mechanism, route distinction or functional relationship.

pages.title: First-pass effect

concepts.label: First-pass metabolism
concepts.detail: Intestinal/hepatic degradation or alteration before general circulation reduces active drug reaching systemic circulation; greater first pass reduces oral systemic availability.
concepts.rationale: Explicit general definition, mechanism, route distinction or functional relationship.

pages.title: Subcutaneous delivery

concepts.label: SC properties
concepts.detail: Simple diffusion; slower than IV, sustained effects possible; blood-flow limitation and poor-circulation influence; irritating drugs unsuitable; minimizes IV-associated hemolysis/thrombosis risks.
